question.problem:
Calculate the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD},$ given the points $A(0,2,-1),$ $B(3,4,1),$ $C(-1,3,2),$ and $D(2,1,0).$

$V=${{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(3i+4j+k)-(2j-k) \\  & =3i+2j+2k \\  & =⟨3,2,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-i+3j+2k)-(2j-k) \\  & =-i+j+3k \\  & =⟨-1,1,3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(2i+j)-(2j-k) \\  & =2i-j+k \\  & =⟨2,-1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(1\cdot 1-3\cdot (-1))-2((-1)\cdot 1-3\cdot 2)+2((-1)\cdot (-1)-1\cdot 2) \\  & =3(1+3)-2(-1-6)+2(1-2) \\  & =12-(-14)-2 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelpiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|24|=24.
$$
